item.title: Transverse Friction for Common Extensor Tendon Region
clinicalUse: Selected lateral elbow tendinopathy as a short-term adjunct to loading
patientPosition: Sitting with elbow supported and forearm relaxed.
therapistPosition: Sit close to the lateral elbow with wrist neutral.
stabilization: Forearm supported so extensor muscles can relax.
contact: Supported fingertip contact over clinically relevant tendon region near lateral epicondyle.
forceDirection: Small transverse movement across tendon fibers rather than sliding along skin.
dosage: Short tolerable bouts, typically 30–90 seconds initially rather than prolonged aggressive friction.
mistakes: Using friction instead of progressive strengthening.
safety: Avoid acute tear, hematoma, skin lesion or uncontrolled bleeding risk.
item.visualCue: Precise tendon contact ↔ small transverse motion → grip re-test.

subTechniques.name: Common Extensor Tendon — Deep Transverse Friction
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Adjunct for selected chronic lateral-elbow tendon pain when the common extensor origin is the familiar symptomatic structure.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Sitting with the forearm supported and elbow flexed comfortably.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the skin over the lateral epicondylar tendon region and place a fingertip/reinforced finger across the tendon fibers.
subTechniques.direction: Use a small transverse movement across the tendon; avoid sliding over the skin or pressing directly on bone.
subTechniques.dosage: Short tolerable bouts only, then progress to wrist-extensor loading.
subTechniques.reassess: Pain-free grip, resisted wrist extension and local tendon tenderness.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: The key outcome is improved loading tolerance, not how sore the tendon becomes during friction.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid acute tear or highly irritable inflammatory presentation.

subTechniques.name: Common Flexor Tendon — Deep Transverse Friction
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Adjunct for selected chronic medial-elbow tendon pain.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Sitting with forearm supported and the medial elbow relaxed.
subTechniques.contact: Precise transverse contact over the flexor-pronator tendon region while protecting the ulnar nerve posterior to the medial epicondyle.
subTechniques.direction: Small transverse movement across the tendon fibers.
subTechniques.dosage: Short symptom-guided bouts followed by graded flexor/pronator loading.
subTechniques.reassess: Resisted wrist flexion/pronation, grip and local tenderness.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Know where the ulnar nerve is before applying pressure around the medial elbow.
